evals.prompt: Resolve the latest LiveBench release and list its discovered categories and subtasks.
evals.expected_output: One compact JSON response resolving latest to an explicit release ID/date and listing dynamically discovered categories and subtasks with source provenance.
expectations: The response cites the official app/data source URL, discovered-from URL, fetched_at, release ID/date, parser/version, and hashes when supplied.
The resolved latest release is explicit on every model/category/subtask row; release mixing is rejected.
Model/provider/variant identity is preserved for category and subtask rows, including explicit null variants.
Overall/category/subtask semantics and aggregation formulas remain source-defined; the overall score is not renamed pass_at_1.
Placeholder values are null/missing with diagnostics and do not become category or subtask scores.
The command never silently falls back to an older release after a failed latest asset; stale data requires an explicit option and is labeled.
Unknown release/category/subtask fields remain under raw_fields/raw_metadata with original labels.
Categories and subtasks are discovered dynamically and the output does not assume a permanent category count/list.

evals.prompt: Compare three model variants on Coding and Agentic Coding while preserving release metadata and cost per successful task.
evals.expected_output: A compact three-variant comparison with separate Coding and Agentic Coding scores, explicit release metadata, published aggregation, and LiveBench cost per successful task.
expectations: Every row preserves official source/discovery URLs, fetched_at, explicit release ID/date/generated_at, parser/version, and source paths.
All three model/provider/variant identities remain distinct and are not merged by display name.
Coding, Agentic Coding, overall, subtask, and cost_per_successful_task semantics stay separate; overall is never called pass_at_1 and cost is never derived from AA/DeepSWE/token prices.
No placeholder score or cost is presented as published; absent values have missing/unparsed status and reasons.
No older release or stale cache is silently substituted; explicit stale mode is visible in scope/provenance.
New provider/model/category fields remain under raw_fields and preserve raw labels.
Both categories are selected from dynamic source categories and a future added category would be accepted without schema-code changes.
Any derived ordering/delta is labeled derived and cannot overwrite published category, overall, or cost values.

evals.prompt: Retrieve a model’s subtask breakdown without calling the overall score pass@1.
evals.expected_output: A compact model/subtask response with release and category scope, source-defined subtask scores, and no pass_at_1 terminology for LiveBench overall.
expectations: Each subtask cites source URL/path, fetched_at, explicit release/version, extraction method, and parser/version.
Model/provider/variant identity is carried through every subtask row.
Subtask score definitions/units are preserved separately from category and overall aggregation; overall is not labeled pass_at_1.
Missing or placeholder subtasks are absent/null with reasons, never synthetic zero values.
A failed refresh cannot silently replace the selected release with stale/older data.
Unknown subtask metadata and labels remain under raw_fields/raw_metadata.
Subtask names are dynamic source data rather than a fixed enum, and a new name is emitted without code changes.
The one-object stdout response keeps operational warnings on stderr and exposes partial extraction explicitly.

evals.prompt: Simulate a broken release asset and prove that the skill does not silently fall back to an older release.
evals.expected_output: A structured non-success JSON envelope containing the attempted release asset URL/status and no rows from another release unless explicit stale mode was requested.
expectations: The error preserves official source/discovery URL, attempted asset URL, fetched_at, selected release/version, HTTP status, parser/version, and relevant hash metadata.
Any retained model/provider/variant identity is clearly scoped to the failed release and no older-release identity is emitted as current.
The failure does not reinterpret the broken asset as a pass_at_1/overall success or fabricate category scores.
404, malformed, and mixed-release fixtures produce structured RELEASE_NOT_FOUND/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE/MALFORMED_PAYLOAD/MIXED_RELEASE diagnostics.
No stale fallback occurs by default; explicit stale mode is marked stale and keeps the requested snapshot/release visible.
Unknown error payload fields and response headers remain in safe raw diagnostics without credentials.
The release/catalog resolver remains dynamic and reports the failed release rather than assuming a permanent release list.
Stdout is exactly one compact ok:false object and stderr contains only operational diagnostics, with no source data masquerading as success.

evals.prompt: Simulate a new category and prove it appears dynamically.
evals.expected_output: A compact catalog/leaderboard response containing the new category's canonical key, original label, score scope, raw metadata, and an unknown-category warning when taxonomy is unfamiliar.
expectations: The new category row cites source/discovery URLs, fetched_at, explicit release/version, extraction method, parser/version, and source path.
Model/provider/variant identity remains intact in the new category row.
Its score remains category_score/unknown according to source semantics and is not called overall or pass_at_1 without source proof.
Placeholder values in the new category are missing/null with a diagnostic, not zero.
The category is sourced from the selected release and is not silently loaded from stale or older release data.
Original category label and unknown metadata are preserved under raw_fields/raw_metadata.
The category appears through dynamic discovery without adding an enum/schema branch; `UNKNOWN_CATEGORY` is emitted only as a diagnostic, not as a reason to drop it.
The CLI emits one compact JSON object with category/release scope and keeps diagnostics on stderr.
